Amazing With Some Feedback. I love this app. I have been using it for roughly 3 and a half years. It really has been a helpful way for me to stay on top of my goals.

 an option to push all of your calendar activities back a day, in case one day is a wash

Either there is a setting where you can add to this list or the presets start appearing on the list every time you add a new activity or routine. This way I do not have to keep re-adding common activities and routines. Nor do I have to make a common activity a routine because it’s not a routine. It’s just something that I do frequently but on no specific days. Also, if you could make sure the picture is associated with the preset. That way I don’t have to find my associated picture every time I make an activity I’ve already used. Also, make it so you can add Duplicates in the Calendar menu. Also, when you add a Duplicate, make sure the picture also remains the same so I don’t have to find and re-add it
 make it easier to turn Project goals into Activities and Routines. Have Project menus where you can see just the Goals, Routines and Activities of individual projects 
 Make a Timer menu where you can see your current Activity or Routine counting down in relation to upcoming Activities ans Routines for that day a la Timeglass app

If you add these features it will really take this app to the next level and I can delete other Scheduling/Productivity apps and just use this one. This is the primary one I use but I still have to switch between apps from time to time because it doesn’t provide any of the aforementioned features above. 

Thank you for your consideration from an avid user and fan of your app.

Sincerely,
David

I really want to love this app. First, why I want to love it
- There is a theory and method behind the system of setting goals that makes sense, has been tested over time, and is powerful and motivating.
- There is calendar integration that sends you daily reminders of what your daily targets are via email: this keeps me connected to my goals and coming back to the app.
- There is a lot of support for the app in the App Store
- There’s a deep knowledge base available when you subscribe to the premium content, which I did.

But here’s the problem, the actual user interface where you set up your goals is unintuitive and frustrating. 

Here’s what I mean. I’m a visual person. I need to see things to understand them. The goal setting and tracking interface is structured like an excel spreadsheet that captures your data. And as we know, apps love data, data is what this is all about. But people don’t think like apps and spreadsheets make me want to chew the walls. 

My goals are constantly shifting because I’m constantly learning and adjusting them, but when I tap in to my goal “cell” to edit it, it doesn’t expand. I can’t see the whole text, just the last line of it. Which means, I have to copy all that text and switch to a text editor to edit it outside the app. 

When you are setting up the goals there are all these data capture fields that mean nothing to me. Target Value, Starting Value, Unit? I have no idea what to do with this. I understand that goals need to be measurable, and I would dearly love the satisfaction of being able to measure my progress over time, but this is so opaque to me. It’s trying to be applicable to every possible scenario, and I’m supposed to know what my specific scenario is in the universe of scenarios. It assumes I’m more of an expert than I am. It would be more helpful if there were a couple of categories of most likely goal possibilities, then shepherd me down that path and make these choices for me so I don’t have to. 

Finally, the check boxes have a kind of visual language that I don’t understand. There was a rounded rectangle with a “p” in the middle of it. I was looking for a way to edit the goal and I tapped that by accident and it disappeared. Oh, that was a check box! It didn’t look like a checkbox, I thought it was a bullet. Where did it go? How do I get it back? Who knows. 

Anyway, I’m getting frustrated with this and even though I’ve pre-paid for a year’s subscription, I’m going to look for other options because I spend more time thinking about how the app works than I do about my goals, and who has time for that?

I hope this feedback is helpful, I’m not trying to be a jerk, just giving you my real experience. I’d love to use this system if only it was more usable.

There are redundant areas within the app and moreover, the website version (for when you're filling things in your responses from a computer) is organized slightly differently-not enough to be obvious, but just enough to confuse you. Despite these shortcomings, the app has been lately undergoing a visual refresh and if you can wade through the layers, you'll find a lot of depth and insight in here.
